defects.source_says: The held Code text jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t19-s3473.txt shows that Pub. L. 116-113 sec. 601 repealed the NAFTA Implementation Act provisions effective July 1, 2020, and that Pub. L. 116-260 div. O sec. 601(a) revived section 533. The claim does not establish from a held current source whether section 543 (22 U.S.C. 290m-2), the statutory object of sections 4-9, survived or was revived. Missing evidence of repeal is offered in place of a current predicate.

reasoning: The genuine version differs from the planted control only in the six first_end dates, now 2005-06-17. That matches the held EO 13380 text ('Executive Order 13380 of June 17, 2005', with no separate effective date) and the claim's own judgment reasons, so the planted defect is gone. All other checks from the blind review carry over: identity, byte-exact quotes, the complete 18-clause inventory, the EO 13380 amendment mapping, and the OFR note being addressed. Two defects remain under the same standard applied to the other claims, so the claim is rejected. First, the EO 14354 later event on section 10 gives the signing date (2025-09-29) as its effective date, but EO 14354 sec. 4 makes the order effective September 30, 2025. Second, the current predicate for the section 543 delegations (sections 3(d) and 4-9) rests on the absence of evidence of repeal. A held Code text (usc-t19-s3473) shows that Pub. L. 116-113 sec. 601 repealed the NAFTA Implementation Act effective July 1, 2020, and that only section 533 is shown revived by Pub. L. 116-260. The survival of section 543 is not established from any held current source.
